_note: Canonical short commands, written by the developer (not by the blind authors) after the first live test: 'come here', 'go there' and a bare 'breach' all fell below the threshold. The blind authors were told NOT to reuse the spec's wording, so the research data has almost no plain, frequent phrasings -- right for testing robustness, wrong for training a bot. These seed lines are added to TRAINING only (train_final.py --seeds, seed_check.py); they are never scored as test lines. Bare nouns that are usually callouts in shooters ('window', 'roof', 'stairs') are left out on purpose. Second round, after the live test showed 'do not come to me' -> FOLLOW_ME 0.93 once the seeds tied 'come' to FOLLOW_ME: negated commands added (NONE; WAIT for 'yet' / 'hold off'). The user's own negated lines are kept out, to test on.
